quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line between the lanes. This tells you:

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
This is a one-way road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken yellow lines can be crossed when it is safe to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal. What should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane shown by the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after giving way to oncoming cars and people walking.
You have the right of way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange
Red
Green
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Brown signs mark public recreation areas and historic or cultural sites. They help you find attractions when traveling in unfamiliar places.

questions.question: What is the best way to merge onto a freeway?

options.text: Drive slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the freeway traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to freeway speed so you can blend in safely. Traffic entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on it.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may move in the direction shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction, but only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before moving in that direction.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane they must move in the direction shown. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you look to check your blind spot?

options.text: Over your right shoulder
In your side mirror
Over your left shoulder
In your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction you are traveling.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether the vehicle is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed area.
You should slow to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell you to slow down. If a new speed limit is shown, that speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes roads slippery. In bad conditions, you may need to drive slower than the speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night driving
Uphill slopes

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the more powerful the impact in a crash.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you should:

options.text: Return to the driving lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the driving lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing a vehicle on a two-lane road, return to the right lane when you have enough space between your vehicle and the one you passed.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and change lanes when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit when entering, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Speed up gently before entering the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum may make it hard to turn, so reducing speed helps you keep control.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but you must let pedestrians and other traffic clear the intersection first.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.
The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
The recommended speed to drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the speed limit, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones and work zones. If weather or road construction makes the speed limit unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: An upcoming intersection.
Road construction.
An upcoming curve in the road.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when one driver does something other drivers do not expect. Tell other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do. Use turn signals when slowing down, stopping, or changing direction. Use your hazard lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: When can you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: You should use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This warns other drivers about the danger.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask oncoming drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if the pedestrian is crossing against the light or being careless.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow showed. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist might have to swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road. Always drive carefully around bicyclists.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Stop completely.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When approaching a roundabout, slow down. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to show drivers which lanes to use for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean no car in either direction can cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass another car over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Go slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. Signal, look for a gap in traffic, speed up to match the traffic speed, then merge into the gap.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings and drivers must always obey them.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on regular streets (not highways, freeways, or subdivision roads) is:

options.text: 25 mph
35 mph
45 mph
55 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on regular streets is 55 mph. Follow posted signs if a different speed limit is shown.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well before your exit. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be moving or stationary.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow). They are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop.
Fines double in a work zone.
Stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
When passing a motorcycle, your vehicle must move completely into the left lane.
A motorcycle's brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, your vehicle must move completely into the left lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane of traffic. Make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Divided highway begins.
A steep grade is ahead.
The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of opposite traffic are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What should you do when a car is coming toward you with bright headlights?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means you may turn in the direction of the arrow.
It tells you a green arrow is coming next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and get ready for a red light.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Heat makes this worse by bringing up more oil.

questions.question: When should you use your parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park.
Only when parking on a hill.
Only when parking in a driveway.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake when you park. Turn off the engine, set the parking brake, and take your keys. Do not rely on the transmission to hold your car in place.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body remove in one hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks.
One alcoholic drink.
Two alcoholic drinks.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on the amount you drink, how fast you drink, your weight, how much food you have eaten, and your health.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because other cars are unlikely to be coming.
By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.
If you have a solid yellow line next to your lane and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass when there is a solid yellow line next to your lane.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: First look left because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again in case you missed a car.

questions.question: What is the first thing to do if you need to slow down on a slippery road?

options.text: Press your brakes firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow down more, gently press your brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield when entering from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: When is it okay to park in an access aisle next to a disability parking space?

options.text: Never.
When you have a disability plate or parking placard.
When all other parking spaces are full.
When you are only parking for a few minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never park in an access aisle. Parking in an access aisle is a traffic violation.
